punchline: The Game Boy's screen had no colour, but it left its rivals behind because it was cheap, sturdy and lasted for hours.
thirty_sec: In 1989, when Nintendo released the Game Boy with a faded screen and old technology, its rivals laughed. Gunpei Yokoi's philosophy was lateral thinking with withered technology: combining cheap, reliable parts creatively. The Game Boy was tough, long-lasting and cheap, and it sold tens of millions. According to David Epstein, Yokoi's strength lay not in the newest but in combining what was at hand in a new way.
